qt: to the Commission Barbara Bonte (PfE) Subject:

On 29 October 2025, the revised trade arrangement between the EU and Ukraine entered into force under the Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area (DCFTA), with greater tariff-free quotas for various sensitive agricultural products. The annual quota for poultry meat was increased from 90 000 to 120 000 tons, and for eggs from 6 000 to 18 000 tons. The additional market access is accompanied by a gradual alignment of Ukraine with EU production standards, including in relation to animal welfare. In its declaration regarding the Council Decision, Belgium stressed that the current differences in animal welfare standards should not continue beyond 2028 and called on the Commission to monitor imports of sensitive products, particularly poultry and eggs, closely and to activate the safeguard clause immediately if necessary. 1.
Does the Commission share Belgium’s view that the differences between the EU and Ukraine regarding animal welfare standards must be eliminated by 2028, at the latest?
How is the Commission actually monitoring Ukraine’s compliance with its obligations regarding alignment with EU standards?

What objective criteria and thresholds is the Commission applying for activation of the safeguard clause if the increased imports of poultry meat or eggs put pressure on the European market or producers?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.10.2026) Pursuant to the reviewed Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area (DCFTA)1, Ukraine has committed to align its legislation with certain EU production standards by the end of 2028. These include EU rules on animal welfare. Ukraine shall report to the Commission every year on its progress in meeting these commitments. Ukraine is also in the process of aligning its national legislation to the EU acquis, including on animal welfare as part of the accession negotiations. However, further work is needed, including on requirements for official controls, plant protection products, contaminants and genetically modified organisms. In this framework, the Commission publishes an annual country report assessing Ukraine’s2 progress towards alignment with the EU acquis. Pursuant to the reviewed DCFTA, the EU may take safeguard measures, if serious economic, societal or environmental difficulties of a sectoral or regional nature liable to persist have arisen or threaten to arise in either Party, including in one or several Member States, as a result of imports of a product covered by the additional reduction of customs duties under the reviewed DCFTA. The Commission closely monitors trade flows between the EU and Ukraine and the evolution of EU agricultural markets, in particular EU production and price trends, among other indicators. There is currently no evidence that the conditions for applying a safeguard measure are met, confirming that the revised quota levels under the reviewed DCFTA are fair and balanced.
